title: Status brief: verification and replay options for streaming degradation
body:
Executive snapshot:

What happened
On 2027-01-09 between ~22:12 UTC and 05:42 UTC (2027-01-10) Redwood experienced elevated rates of truncated and stalled streaming responses for a subset of hosted API tenants. The root cause was a race in our streaming fanout layer that under certain load patterns returned partial event batches to clients while downstream token assembly lagged, causing some streaming sessions to terminate early or show gaps.

Who was affected
- ~3.4% of active tenants saw at least one affected session during the window.
- Impacted features: streaming text generation (chunked responses) and the streaming portion of chat_sessions using model variants X-1 and X-2 in us-west and eu-west regions.
- Non-impacted: non-streaming generation, embeddings, and Dedicated private clusters not using the shared fanout path.

Customer-facing impact (plain language)
If you use our streaming API (events delivered as chunks) you may have observed:
- responses that stopped mid-sentence,
- missing intermediate chunks and then a final truncated result, or
- clients that reported connection closed without a final event.

Immediate operator action taken
- 22:30 UTC: throttled the global streaming fanout to limit concurrent per-connection batches.
- 23:05 UTC: deployed a conservative patch that enforced ordered delivery semantics for in-flight token batches.
- 01:15–02:00 UTC: gradual rollback of the most aggressive batching heuristics while we validated throughput impact.
- 05:42 UTC: monitoring showed error rates and chunk-drop counts returned to baseline; full validation completed by 07:00 UTC.

Current status
- Service: available. Streaming is operating within normal parameters.
- Residual risk: low. We continue to monitor for any re-occurrence and are throttling a small experimental batching policy until further testing is complete.

How you can verify whether you were affected (step-by-step)
We provide two verification paths: quick checks and an evidence package request.

1) Quick SDK/API check (5 minutes)
- Check your request logs for any streaming request with start time between 2027-01-09T22:12:00Z and 2027-01-10T05:42:00Z and response_size_tokens < expected tokens for your prompt.
- Example curl to fetch recent requests (replace TENANT_KEY and FILTER times):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer TENANT_KEY" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/self/requests?from=2027-01-09T22:00:00Z&to=2027-01-10T06:00:00Z&kind=streaming"
- Look for entries where response.status = "partial" or response.stream_closed_early = true.

2) Self-validate a single session (replay on your side)
- If you retain the prompt and request_id from the window you observed, re-run the request against the current streaming endpoint using the same model and parameters to see if the output now completes.
- Example (node):
  // simple sample: re-issue the same streaming request and compare final token count
  // This assumes deterministic or near-deterministic prompts; for non-deterministic models, compare presence/absence of truncation rather than exact token sequence.

3) Request an evidence package from Redwood (recommended for high-impact tenants)
- If you need definitive proof for a set of requests, open a support case with subject: "Evidence package request: streaming gap window 2027-01-09" and include up to 10 request_ids and the tenant id. Our triage team will provide:
  - server-side event logs for the session(s),
  - token assembly timelines and fanout traces, and
  - a short analyst note explaining whether the specific request exhibited the known race.
- We aim to deliver evidence packages within 48 hours of a validated request.

Replay and reconciliation choices for tenants
We offer three customer options depending on your integration and tolerance for reprocessing:
- Opt-in replay (recommended for critical workflows): Redwood can re-run affected requests server-side where possible and return regenerated outputs or a delta summary. Requires tenant consent and is limited to idempotent/side-effect-free workloads.
- Client-side replay: For prompt-only workflows, re-issuing requests from your side is simplest and recommended. Use idempotency tokens where your application needs dedup protection.
- No-replay / compensating action: For stateful or side-effectful flows, we recommend applying compensating transactions rather than blind replays. Contact your account team for guidance.

How to request a Redwood opt-in replay
1) Open a support ticket and include: tenant id, list of request_ids (max 50), desired output shape (full response vs summary), and whether you allow re-generation with the same model variant or accept a compatible fallback.
2) Our replay team will validate idempotency constraints and produce either: a) re-generated outputs packaged with confidence notes, or b) a curated reconciliation summary if replay is unsafe.
3) Expected turnaround: 48–96 hours depending on request volume and prioritization.

Assurances about data integrity and privacy
- No customer data was exposed to other tenants. The bug was internal to the fanout/delivery path; we found no evidence of cross-tenant leakage.
- Logs and evidence packages are provided only to authorized tenant contacts and under existing data access controls.

Root cause (concise technical explanation)
A recently-introduced batching optimization attempted to improve per-token throughput by merging multiple in-flight token fragments for the same downstream socket. Under a specific interleaving of small responses and timeouts, merged fragments could be emitted while downstream assembly state lagged, leading to lost or out-of-order finalization events. The patch rolled out on 2027-01-09 contained an ordering check regression.

Remediation and prevention actions
Already completed:
- Reverted the ordering regression and introduced stricter unit and integration tests for streaming delivery ordering.
- Added canary traffic gating for batching heuristics by tenant and region.
Planned in the next 90 days:
- Strengthen end-to-end deterministic replay tests using synthetic and real tenant traffic.
- Implement an adaptive back-pressure signal from downstream assembly to the fanout layer.
- Add a tenant-visible header in streaming events (x-rw-stream-ack) to help customers confirm full completion of a logical stream on their side.

Compensation and SLA considerations
- If you experienced measurable impact to your SLA (for tenants under a formal SLA), your Customer Success / Account team will reach out with tailored remediation and credit proposals.
- For tenants without an SLA, we will evaluate replay feasibility and offer credits on a case-by-case basis.

Recommended customer configuration changes to reduce future surface area
- Use idempotency tokens for any request that can cause side effects.
- For critical streaming consumers, subscribe to both chunked streaming and periodic finalization callbacks (a small polling endpoint) so you have a definitive completion signal.
- Implement client-side timeout/retry backoff with exponential jitter and detect "partial" completion flags that our SDKs will return when present.

Support contacts and next steps
- Primary contact for this incident: Maya Chen (Customer Success Lead) — maya.chen@redwood.ai
- For urgent tenant evidence requests: support@redwood.ai (include "Evidence package: 2027-01-09 streaming" in subject).
- Account teams will proactively reach out to tenants identified as high-impact. If you want to opt into proactive replay even if you were not marked, reply to this thread or file a ticket.

Appendix: example evidence request template (copy/paste)
- Subject: Evidence package request: streaming gap 2027-01-09
- Tenant ID: <your-tenant-id>
- Contact: name, email, phone
- Request ids (comma-separated, max 50): <rid_1,rid_2,...>
- Desired outcome: "replay" or "evidence-only"

Internal note (for CS operators)
- Tag support ticket with JIRA-INC-2027-4127 and route to "replay-team".
- Use redwood-evidence-tool to generate per-request packet prior to sending to customers.

Closing
We know interruptions like this cost you time and trust. Our engineering and CS teams treated this as a high-priority reliability issue and focused on both immediate mitigation and long-term safeguards. We will publish a full public postmortem once all follow-ups and testing are complete; this note is intended to help you validate impact and choose the appropriate reconciliation path for your application.
